title: Targeting Aberrant Expression of STAT3 and AP-1 Oncogenic Transcription Factors and HPV Oncoproteins in Cervical Cancer by Berberis aquifolium.
authors: Singh, Tejveer; Chhokar, Arun; Thakur, Kulbhushan; Aggarwal, Nikita; Pragya, Pragya; Yadav, Joni; Tripathi, Tanya; Jadli, Mohit; Bhat, Anjali; Gupta, Pankaj; Khurana, Anil; Chandra Bharti, Alok
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物对宫颈癌细胞中STAT3/AP-1及HPV E6/E7表达的影响，仅含少量分子对接，非蛋白质-DNA互作核心体系，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: Background: Present study examines phytochemical preparation that uses berberine's plant source B. aquifolium root for availability of similar anti-cervical cancer (CaCx) and anti-HPV activities to facilitate repurposing of the B. aquifolium based drug in the treatment of CaCx. Purpose: To evaluate therapeutic potential of different concentrations of ethanolic extract of B. aquifolium root mother tincture (BAMT) against HPV-positive (HPV16: SiHa, HPV18: HeLa) and HPV-negative (C33a) CaCx cell lines at molecular oncogenic level. Materials and Methods: BAMT was screened for anti-proliferative activity by MTT assay. Cell cycle progression was analyzed by flowcytometry. Then, the expression level of STAT3, AP-1, HPV E6 and E7 was detected by immunoblotting, whereas nuclear localization was observed by fluorescence microscopy. Phytochemicals reportedly available in BAMT were examined for their inhibitory action on HPV16 E6 by in silico molecular docking. Results: BAMT induced a dose-dependent decline in CaCx cell viability in all cell types tested. Flowcytometric evaluation of BAMT-treated cells showed a small but specific cell growth arrest in G1-phase. BAMT-treatment resulted in reduced protein expression of key transcription factors, STAT3 with a decline of its active form pSTAT3 (Y705); and components of AP-1 complex, JunB and c-Jun. Immunocytochemistry revealed that BAMT did not prevent the entry of remnant active transcription factor to the nucleus, but loss of overall transcription factor activity resulted in reduced availability of transcription factors in the cancer cells. These changes were accompanied by gradual loss of HPV E6 and E7 protein in BAMT-treated HPV-positive cells. Molecular docking of reported active phytochemicals in B. aquifolium root was performed, which indicated a potential interference of HPV16 E6's interaction with pivotal cellular targets p53, E6AP or both by constituent phytochemicals. Among these, berberine, palmatine and magnoflorine showed highest E6 inhibitory potential. Conclusion: Overall, BAMT showed multi-pronged therapeutic potential against HPV infection and cervical cancer and the study described the underlying molecular mechanism of its action.
abstract_zh: 背景：本研究考察了利用小檗碱的植物来源B. aquifolium根制备的植物化学制剂，以评估其是否具有类似的抗宫颈癌（CaCx）和抗HPV活性，从而促进基于B. aquifolium的药物在CaCx治疗中的再利用。目的：评估不同浓度的B. aquifolium根母酊剂（BAMT）乙醇提取物对HPV阳性（HPV16：SiHa，HPV18：HeLa）和HPV阴性（C33a）CaCx细胞系在分子致癌水平上的治疗潜力。材料与方法：通过MTT实验筛选BAMT的抗增殖活性。利用流式细胞术分析细胞周期进程。随后，通过免疫印迹检测STAT3、AP-1、HPV E6和E7的表达水平，而核定位通过荧光显微镜观察。据报道BAMT中存在的植物化学物质通过计算机分子对接检测其对HPV16 E6的抑制作用。结果：BAMT在所有测试细胞类型中诱导CaCx细胞活力呈剂量依赖性下降。流式细胞术评估显示，BAMT处理的细胞在G1期出现小而特异的细胞生长停滞。BAMT处理导致关键转录因子STAT3及其活性形式pSTAT3（Y705）的蛋白表达降低，以及AP-1复合物组分JunB和c-Jun的表达减少。免疫细胞化学显示，BAMT并未阻止残留活性转录因子进入细胞核，但整体转录因子活性的丧失导致癌细胞中转录因子可用性降低。这些变化伴随着BAMT处理的HPV阳性细胞中HPV E6和E7蛋白的逐渐丧失。对B. aquifolium根中已报道的活性植物化学物质进行分子对接，结果表明其组成植物化学物质可能干扰HPV16 E6与关键细胞靶点p53、E6AP或两者的相互作用。其中，小檗碱、巴马汀和木兰花碱显示出最高的E6抑制潜力。结论：总体而言，BAMT显示出针对HPV感染和宫颈癌的多方面治疗潜力，本研究描述了其作用的潜在分子机制。
